newsitem.title: BELGIUM: TENNIS-RIVALRY WITH RUSEDSKI IS GOOD FOR BRITISH GAME - HENMAN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RIVALRY WITH RUSEDSKI IS GOOD FOR BRITISH GAME - HENMAN.

text.p: British number one Tim Henman said on Tuesday that his rivalry with compatriot Greg Rusedski stimulated both players and would boost Britain's Davis Cup potential.

"When he was ranked above me he spurred me on and...I set my target to try and overtake him. Now that I've done that I'm sure it is a very positive rivalry," Henman said after his 6-3 4-6 6-4 first-round win over Spain's Sergi Bruguera in the European Community championship.
Henman is ranked 19th in the world, 17 places above Rusedski.
"Rusedski has probably seen the way I started off in Australia where he didn't play particularly well and now he has bounced back with two finals and that definitely gives me a big lift.
"I think we can both feed off each other and I think it bodes well for the Davis Cup," Henman said.

Rusedski suffered first round defeats early this year in Auckland and at the Australian Open but has since reached finals in Zagreb and San Jose, losing to Goran Ivanisevic and to world number one Pete Sampras respectively.
Henman won the Sydney International tournament last month, his first professional title, and reached the third round of the Australian Open.
